title: never works, various error messages: G6 SENSOR FAILED, G6 Start Failed; No signal
body:
I've gone through 3 rounds of troubleshooting, calling in friends and random people from the internet, spending hours trying to get this app to work. I'm not a technical idiot but it's extremely difficult to isolate any one issue and troubleshoot. I've heard wonderful things about the app and I hate spending $25 every 10 days, so I'd love to figure it out.

I've checked for all the usual problem settings, stopped and restarted, etc. 
I thought I had it working yesterday when I switched from the official Dexcom app a day before  the sensor expired: it worked until the sensor expired, started the restart process and got about to 1.5 hours remaining before failing. This happened 3 times with me adjusting settings, calibrating, etc. This was the longest period of time I've gotten it to work. 
Last week when I was troubleshooting it was saying my number was 288 for about two days.

I'm extremely frustrated! 

Other factors:
- I can't restart sensors anymore with any of the Dexcom hacks, ever since I replaced the transmitter.
- I have a Samsung Galaxy S7
- The first two digits of my transmitter are 81
- The first two numbers of my current sensor are 59, but the app has failed with every sensor I've tried, even that start with the 91. 
- I check G6 in the startup wizard
- I've granted battery optimization
- OB1 and Native Algorithm are both checked
- I don't have a smart watch

Happy to supply any additional information, please help

comments.body: Unfortunately Preemptive restarts doesn't work with the 81 transmitters you will need to uncheck it. Sensor will die at 10 days unfortunately with preemptive restarts unchecked.

So 81 transmitters can't be restarted at all? 
Because it wasn't a preemptive restart, just a regular restart.

I'm using 81... transmitter and have no issue with preemptive restart.  Just happened yesterday, still going strong... Pixel 2xl.

my setup has "restart sensor" checked, then under the preemptive restarts section I have the top three of the four checked.

Can you give more info on what specifically happens?  At day 10 what happens?  For me, it's a totally hands-off process. It just restarts, puts a little flag looking symbol on the graph and that's it.

Sure, sorry for the vagueness, I've just tried so many things so many times over time that it's hard to describe/remember what I've done and what happens. 
I've never had it work for 10 days. It will work for maybe a couple readings, except for the other day when it worked for about a day. 
Attempts 1 and 2: this was after the sensor in me was already expired. I would uninstall the official app and attempt to get more life out of the sensor with XDrip. I would get one or two readings after warmup, but then a "signal loss" or "can't communicate with sensor" or "sensor reporting failed" or "sensor failed start" errors, even though it had been communicating fine in the official Dexcom app. I'll try restarting my sensor now to see what error it gives so I can be really specific. (right now it says "sensor is still warming up, please wait" at the top which is expected, but at the bottom it says "sensor failed start" already, which might be leftover from a previous attempt?)
Attempt yesterday: I uninstalled Dexcom and started X Drip on Day 9, and it was working fine until Day 10. It started to restart but then about an hour in it failed. I tried restarting and it asked for calibrations but then rejected them and remained dead.

ok so I just tried to restart it, it warmed up for about 20 minutes, then sent a "Session Start Failing: Invalid error". when I opened it app it was asking for two calibrations which I did, and it appears that it had three readings right before the calibrations. no readings after the calibrations, but did send a "calibration rejected: sensor stopped" error.
i had the exact same issue. Turning off preemptive restarts fixed it for me. Try it and see if it will work. I guess some of the transmitters work with it and some do not

I turned off pre-emptive restarts, it asked for calibrations which i entered and then about 3 minutes later it says "calibration rejected:sensor stopped". :(
Is there something that is telling the program that the sensor is stopped? could it be the notifications on my phone that I can't seem to swipe away?

You are entering the sensor code in the beginning?. I've noticed on my transmitter if i stop a sensor after the 2hr start it will not work again. So maybe that sensor is having that issue try a new sensor with preemptive restarts off.

I don't want to jinx it, but it miiiight be working now.

steps I took:
- uninstalled a couple security apps from an old job I had
- uninstalling and reinstalling XDrip
- letting it warm up, entering 2 calibrations, then received a "sensor fail error"
- BUT about 1.5 hours later it appears to be sending actual readings. This is after the warm-up session should be done, but it was throwing the sensor fail error that whole time so I kinda lost hope

Fingers crossed that it sticks (pun intended?) Thank you all so much

edit: with pre-emptive restarts switched off, and an old sensor

That is weird man, mine never asks for calibrations but glad that yours is working. You can also turn off ob1 mode and use it like a g5 if all else fails but you will need to calibrate like you did with the g5. This also works past the 10 days I've noticed.

I've been dealing with the same issues for a few weeks now. Switched to a new transmitter with an 81 serial and have been unable to start or restart sensors ever since.

The log just says "Session Start Failed: Invalid" with no further information.
Sometimes this error happens immediately, and sometimes it gets about 30 minutes into warmup and then fails. In the latter case, I get the behavior described in [this issue](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/issues/1104), where it prompts for calibrations (despite being configured to use native algorithm) and then rejects them because the sensor is stopped.

I'm currently using a nightly build from a few days ago and the issue persists; I'm still unable to start sensors.
